text: "Resistance Is Futile" is the ninth episode of the second season and twenty-first overall episode of the American television drama series Dexter, which first aired on November 25, 2007 on Showtime in the United States. The episode was written by Melissa Rosenberg, who earned her fifth writing credit, and directed by Marcos Siega, who received his second directing credit. Set in Miami, the series follows Dexter Morgan, a forensic technician specializing in bloodstain pattern analysis for the fictional Miami Metro Police Department, who leads a secret parallel life as a vigilante serial killer, hunting down murderers who have not been adequately punished by the justice system due to corruption or legal technicalities. In this episode, Dexter discovers that the FBI is following him and that Doakes has taken his blood slides. While staying guard outside her house, Dexter (Michael C. Hall) apologizes to Rita (Julie Benz) for his affair with Lila (Jaime Murray). He drives off to dispose of Jimenez's body at the cabin but finds a car following him; the car belongs to the FBI, and agents check his office to examine the blood work database. In Port-au-Prince, Doakes meets with a friend, Leones (Peter Macon), asking him to analyze Dexter's blood slides, but he does not have them. Dexter realizes the slides are missing and believes Lundy (Keith Carradine) has them. FBI agents arrive and ask him to accompany them to the department, where Lundy and Matthews (Geoff Pierson) await him with the blood slides. Dexter believes he has been caught until Lundy and Matthews state they suspect Doakes is the Bay Harbor Butcher, having raided his car and found the slides. To cover himself, Dexter agrees with their theory, allowing the FBI to protect him while appointing him to analyze the blood slides, during which he uses the opportunity to cover his fingerprints. Despite Dexter's warning, Lila flirts with Angel (David Zayas) and goes out with him and others from the station for drinks, forcing Dexter to go along with them as he fears she will expose his connection to Jimenez. Doakes contacts LaGuerta (Lauren Vélez) to claim his innocence, which she believes. Doakes refuses to surrender and sets out to find evidence, destroying his cell phone in the process. When Lundy plans to reveal Doakes as the prime suspect to the press, LaGuerta tries to get Debra (Jennifer Carpenter) to act, leading to an argument in which Debra yells that she is in a relationship with Lundy. That night, Dexter escapes from his apartment and uses his boat to return to the cabin, where he chops Jimenez's body. As he leaves with the bags, he is held at gunpoint by Doakes, who tracks him with a GPS in the boat. Having discovered the trash bags, Dexter realizes he is the Butcher. Doakes forces Dexter to handcuff himself and walk toward him, but Dexter attacks him. During the fight, Dexter is shot in the leg and they fall into the water, where Dexter uses the handcuffs to knock Doakes unconscious. Doakes later wakes up inside a cage in the cabin, and Dexter locks the door behind him. In its original American broadcast, the episode was seen by an estimated 1.03 million household viewers and gained a 0.5 ratings share among adults aged 18–49, meaning 0.5 percent of all households with televisions watched it. This represented a 17% decrease in viewership from the previous episode, which was watched by an estimated 1.23 million household viewers with a 0.6/1 in the 18–49 demographics. The episode received critical acclaim, with Eric Goldman of IGN giving it an "amazing" 9.5 out of 10, praising it as a nailbiting, suspenseful scenario that felt like the penultimate episode of the season. Scott Tobias of The A.V. Club gave it a "B+" grade, noting that each solution created new problems and that the showdown with Doakes was a surprising reversal of their cat-and-mouse dynamic. Alan Sepinwall wrote that while the episode wasn't bad, it was the first time viewers were genuinely concerned about the show's forward plan, and that the writers' strings were visible. Paula Paige of TV Guide called Michael C. Hall's expressions award-worthy and noted that his self-reflection was unhealthy, while the killing made him more attractive. Keith McDuffee of TV Squad stated it was not surprising that Doakes was brought in as the prime suspect due to prior clues, including taking the blood slides and Doakes' father being a butcher, but was surprised when Doakes appeared on the dock at the end. Television Without Pity gave the episode an "A" grade. Lauren Vélez submitted this episode for consideration for Outstanding Supporting Actress in a Drama Series at the 60th Primetime Emmy Awards.
